tone_statements.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien Language History (Pacific Linguistics 613; Studies in Language Change 8). Canberra: Pacific Linguistics, Australian National University. 298 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Complex contour tones occur almost exclusively in reflexes of category B. This can be understood as a ‘gear-switching’ adjustment required in the mid-syllable transition from modal to creaky (B1) and from breathy to creaky (B2). ... Examples of complex contour tones from Wang and Mao 1995 (WM), Niederer 1998 (N), and Chang 1972 (C) appear below: (11) ... B2 complex tones (< breathy-creaky) ... Luoxiang Mien (WM #17) 213 / Changping Mien (WM #18) 121 / Hsing-an Yao (C #63) 231
tone_statements.locator: p. 196, ch. 3 §3.3.4 'Complex contour tones as phonation gear switches', example (11)
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Only one datum: Changping Mien (Biao Mon) tone B2 (tone 4) = 121, a complex (falling-rising) contour attributed historically to a breathy-to-creaky phonation transition; forms elsewhere are cited with the 8 Mienic tone categories (checked tones 7/8 with stop finals). No inventory, TBU, sandhi or stress statement for this lect.

sources.citation: Taguchi, Yoshihisa 田口善久. 2010. 恭城県三江郷ミエン語(チャウコンメン)調査報告 [A brief sketch of Cao Kong Meng]. 千葉大学ユーラシア言語文化論集 12: 71-82.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; §2.4 声調 (pp. 76-77) gives 7 tone categories and a phonetic tone alternation (tone 3 -> [33] before other tones). Describes Cao Kong Meng = 交公勉 of Shikou village, which Chinese sources group with Biao Min 标敏 (i.e. bje, not bmt). Read for identity: p. 72 fn. 7 says Taguchi 2005 treats the phonology of the neighbouring 'Mohimu' [mo55 çi31 muə31] variety (Litian/Xiaolitian/Niuweizhai villages) and calls it phylogenetically close to Iu Mien.

sources.citation: Taguchi, Yoshihisa 田口善久. 1999. 三江小栗田勉語語彙集 [A study of the vocabulary of Xiaolitian Yao language]. 言語文化論叢 (Papers on Languages and Cultures, Chiba University) 5: 1-28.
sources.note: §1 音韻体系 (pp. 2-3) covers consonants, glides, vowels, finals and tones only; no mention of stress/accent. Only prosodic remark (§1.5, p. 3): the original 8 Mienic tones have merged to 5, and in nouns the tone value of a syllable read in isolation or word-initially differs clearly from its value in non-initial syllables (e.g. tone 1 433/33, tone 2 55/31). Variety: Mien of Xiaolitian, Daliitian, Niuwei villages, Sanjiang township, Gongcheng county (= Taguchi 2005's 'Sanjiang Shimen Mian', which Glottolog files under bmt; identity with Biao Mon proper doubtful).

sources.citation: Luang-Thongkum, Theraphan. 1993. A view on Proto-Mjuenic (Yao). Mon-Khmer Studies 22: 163-230.
sources.note: Image-only PDF; pp. 163-166 (abstract, background, list of field sites) read as page scan: comparative reconstruction from the author's own field data; nothing on stress in the pages read. Its 'Muen' = Ao Yao / Bjao Muen of Jinxiu county (Luoxiang, Liucang), i.e. Ao Biao, not Biao Mon proper (Wikipedia's equation of Muen with Biao Mon is not what the paper says).

sources.note: Not opened (print). Changping, whose B2 (tone 4) reflex is a complex contour 121 (Ratliff 2010:196, ex. 11, 'Changping Mien (WM #18) 121'); pp. 13-16 characterise the Mienic dialect groups by final consonants, voiceless sonorants, vowel length and 'whether or not there is tone sandhi' and state glottal stop occurs only in checked tones 7 and 8 (Aumann & Sidwell 2004:17-19). The only primary tone data on Biao Mon outside Mao 2004 and Tang 1994.
